findings.detail: 'managed_static_type_state.readying' (`state->readying`) is accessed under a critical section at start_readying:489 but is read plainly here, with nothing synchronising it. A lock held by only some accessors of a field serialises nothing: the guarded and unguarded accessors race each other. This is the shape of gh-153298 (ga_parameters / CPY-0025), gh-128714 (func.__annotations__ / CPY-0029) and gh-153908 (itertools count_repr). Py_ssize_t does not tear on LP64, so the visible effect is a stale value rather than memory unsafety — one FT_ATOMIC_* on each access is the fix. Guarded twin: start_readying:489.

'type' becomes reachable from other threads at add_all_subclasses() (line 1966), and 'tp_base' is still written afterwards, in this function, with a plain non-atomic store and no critical section. On a free-threaded build another thread can observe the object between the two — half-initialised, and torn if the store is wider than a word. Finish initialising before publishing, or make the tail stores atomic. This is the fixup_slot_dispatchers shape (gh-151377).

Lazy init of 'type->tp_dealloc' guarded only by a NULL check, with no critical section. Under free-threading two threads both observe NULL and both compute/store -> leak + torn/lost write (cf. descr_get_qualname / TSAN-0043). Guard with Py_BEGIN_CRITICAL_SECTION or a compare-exchange.

_sample.method: the scanner was RE-RUN over exactly these files; every count in this report is sample-scoped. This is not a post-hoc filter of a corpus-wide scan -- a filtered report keeps corpus-wide denominators next to sample-scoped findings, which makes an unearned zero look earned.
